_about: Wire frames of the upstream OpenClaw gateway at tag v2026.10.33 (github.com/openclaw/openclaw), rebuilt from that tag's own unit tests and adapted for sessionKey/runId namespacing. Each scenario pins one interpretation contract documented in docs/UPSTREAM_INTERPRETATION.md. Source file:line is cited per scenario; those citations are recorded in bridge/protocol/openclaw/citations.json and checked by test/upstream-citations.test.ts, and the frames are replayed by test/upstream-frames.test.ts — do not edit shapes without re-checking the upstream tag. ONLY_AT. A scenario carrying `only_at` holds a shape that the tag it names pins and v2026.10.33 does not (the upstream test was removed, or the gateway's copy changed), kept because that version is still supported: its citations are read at THAT tag, `only_at_why` says what replaced it, and the replay test refuses an `only_at` that is the reference tag or has no reason. NOT EVERY FRAME IS COPIED. A `seq` is ours wherever the cited test does not show one, and a content block's `type`/`role` is added where an upstream matcher pins only the text. Composed throughout, and saying so in their description: writer-claim-rebound-after-content, writer-claim-rebound-before-generation, writer-claim-rebound-after-start-zero-content. Composed in part: aborted-user-stop-partial-text (the terminal frame is upstream's, the preceding delta is not), init-conflict-zero-content and init-conflict-zero-content-9.36 (the message is verbatim, the wire frame around it is ours), compaction-explicit-stream-signals (both signals are anchored, the deltas between them are synthetic), error-timeout-stopreason-precedence and aborted-tool-validation-errormessage (the terminal is the test's expected projection, a matcher), error-timeout-with-message-9.36 (same), error-rate-limit-kind-with-overloaded-detail (the three pinned fields and the errorDetail are the test's, a matcher), error-errorkind-rate-limit (the errorMessage text is ours: the upstream test pins only that it contains `Too many requests`), agent-assistant-append-only (lifecycle end and final envelope are ours around the two pinned frames), error-state-contention-dispatch and error-state-contention-dispatch-9.36 (the message is the production literal, the frame is broadcastChatError's), status-waiting-for-state-then-resume (the status and the delta are the Control UI test's, the final is ours), aborted-then-save-warning-error and aborted-then-save-warning-error-9.36 (two cited frames put on one run), chat-delta-replace-retracts-text (the three payloads are the test's matcher), run-status-retrying-reason-retry-at (one attempt of the test's loop, then a delta and a final of ours). chat-send-ack-accepted-queued holds an RPC answer (`ack`), not event frames.

aborted-user-stop-partial-text.description: src/gateway/chat-abort.test.ts:406-442 — a killed run broadcasts state:aborted with a free-form stopReason ('user' is a caller value, NOT in any enum) and the partial text snapshot (shape unchanged since v2026.9.5). The turn must finalize aborted on state alone; stopReason must never reclassify it.

aborted-tool-validation-errormessage.description: src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts:1830-1842 (case `safe validation diagnostic`, projected on lifecycle end by src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts:1875-1894) — self-abort on tool-validation failure: state:aborted carries stopReason:'aborted' plus errorMessage. An aborted turn keeps its abort status; the errorMessage is diagnostic, never a persisted error.

payload.errorMessage: edit tool validation failed: edits: must be an array

error-timeout-stopreason-precedence.description: src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts:1854-1859 (case `timeout without error text`) — a timed-out abort (lifecycle end aborted:true stopReason:'timeout' timeoutPhase:'idle') is emitted as state:ERROR, not aborted: the gateway consumes stopReason BEFORE emitting, and badges the class it recorded as errorKind:'timeout'. At v2026.10.33 the pinned terminal carries NO errorMessage (the case has no error text); the form with a message is error-timeout-with-message-9.36.

error-timeout-with-message-9.36.description: src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts:3776-3803 — the same timed-out abort WITH its error text: lifecycle end aborted:true stopReason:'timeout' timeoutPhase:'provider' error:'agent provider timeout' reaches the wire as state:error, errorKind:'timeout', errorMessage 'agent provider timeout' and NO `message` (the test asserts its absence).
error-timeout-with-message-9.36.only_at_why: v2026.10.33 folded this test into a table whose timeout case has no error text (error-timeout-stopreason-precedence); the projection of an error text beside errorKind is no longer pinned by an upstream test there.

error-rate-limit-kind-with-overloaded-de.description: src/gateway/server-chat.native-provider-error.test.ts:55-103 — the only chat error carrying errorKind:'rate_limit' that a v2026.10.33 gateway test pins: a native provider failure ('Selected model is at capacity…', not aborted) reaches the wire as state:error with errorKind:'rate_limit', the gateway's reader-facing errorMessage and errorDetail {provider, model, failoverReason:'overloaded'} (the gateway folds `overloaded` into the `rate_limit` kind; the classifier is pinned by src/gateway/server-chat.error-kind.test.ts:14). The three fields and the errorDetail are the test's matcher; the seq is ours. CONTRACT: the provider observation outranks the kind — the bridge reads the more precise `overloaded` and classes the turn provider_internal, not rate_limit.

payload.errorMessage: ⚠️ Selected model is at capacity. Try a different model, or wait and retry.

error-errorkind-rate-limit.description: src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts:4505-4532 — a 429 lifecycle error reaches the wire as state:error with errorKind:'rate_limit'. The upstream test asserts the payload has NO `message` and NO `errorDetail` (that field only appears when the runtime recorded a provider observation). The allowlisted wire errorKind survives as the message errorKind. The errorMessage TEXT of the frame is ours, not upstream's: the upstream test pins only that errorMessage contains `Too many requests` (the gateway renders the error with formatForLog), so only the errorKind and the absent message/errorDetail are upstream facts here.
error-errorkind-rate-limit.only_at_why: that test is gone at v2026.10.33, where the only pinned rate_limit chat error also carries an errorDetail (error-rate-limit-kind-with-overloaded-detail).

payload.errorMessage: Provider call failed: 429 Too many requests

writer-claim-rebound-after-content.description: COMPOSED (not copied from one upstream test) — the 2026.8.1+ successor of the 7.1 embedded prompt-lock takeover, which no longer exists (transcripts moved to SQLite). Parts, each cited: the message is thrown verbatim by src/config/sessions/session-transcript-writer-claim-error.ts:46-51 (SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError; the class moved out of transcript-write-context.ts, text identical 8.1->10.33); the error NAME is pinned by src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts:519; the wire rendering '<Name>: <message>' is formatForLog's (src/gateway/ws-log.ts:126-137, pinned for message-like objects by src/gateway/ws-log.test.ts:246-253), and server-chat.ts:899 emits it as errorMessage on state:error. CONTRACT: unlike the 7.1 lock flavour, this one is NOT downgraded to complete — upstream's announce delivery retry loop may retry it (subagent-announce-delivery-retry.ts:97-133 isTransientAnnounceDeliveryError, used at subagent-announce-delivery-retry.ts:189: no retry on send evidence, then a typed retryability decides when present, then a permanent error refuses, and only then a writer rebound retries); a failed direct delivery is `ambiguous` on send evidence and otherwise, for this rebound, `retryable` unless a typed retryability decides otherwise (subagent-announce-direct-delivery.ts:686-690 via isPermanentAnnounceDeliveryError, defined at subagent-announce-delivery-retry.ts:135-141 — CHANGED at v2026.10.33: through v2026.9.36 that function also returned true for a writer rebound, which made the failed direct delivery `permanent_failure`; the regex at subagent-announce-delivery-retry.ts:55-56 is only the shared definition). Atrium keeps the honest error card and classifies the turn session_write_conflict — its OWN class, NOT the retryable session_init_conflict: upstream throws the same text at commits after the model ran (tools may have had external effects) as well as before generation; here content has streamed, which proves the run generated, so Atrium's bounded auto-retry must not re-dispatch it (the pre-generation case is writer-claim-rebound-before-generation).

payload.errorMessage: SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError: session writer claim changed before transcript persistence

writer-claim-rebound-before-generation.description: COMPOSED — the same rebound thrown while the attempt is still PREPARED: src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/session-bootstrap.ts:377-383 (inside prepareInitialSessionWriter, reached from run/session-prompt-state.ts:60) and run/pre-persisted-user-turn.ts:280 (preparePersistedCurrentUserTurn, from run/attempt-session-prepare.ts:597), both before the agent loop emits agent_start (packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.ts:100) — which embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle.ts:87-94 turns into {stream:'lifecycle', data:{phase:'start'}}. The prelude frames (chat state:'status', agent stream:'run_status') are the shapes captured on every run of a full 2026.9.4 bench run, which showed nothing else before lifecycle start; the terminal frame is as in writer-claim-rebound-after-content. CONTRACT: no generation frame on an unbroken stream proves the rebound pre-generation, so the bridge upgrades it to the retryable session_init_conflict and keeps session_write_conflict on the trace channel.

payload.errorMessage: SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError: session writer claim changed before transcript persistence

writer-claim-rebound-after-start-zero-co.description: COMPOSED — the dangerous twin of writer-claim-rebound-before-generation: the run STARTED (lifecycle start, shape as captured on 2026.9.4 and emitted by embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle.ts:93) and then rebounded at a commit with NOTHING visible — the post-generation throws of run/settled-turn-finalization.ts:614,661 come after the attempt. Zero content does not mean no work: tools may have had external effects. CONTRACT: stays session_write_conflict, never auto-retried.

payload.errorMessage: SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError: session writer claim changed before transcript persistence

init-conflict-zero-content.description: src/auto-reply/reply/session-init-conflict-retry.ts:11-14,18-19 — the pre-generation OCC init conflict. CHANGED at v2026.10.33: the message ends with `; please retry your message.` (the retry classifier accepts both endings; the string form without it is still retried, src/auto-reply/reply/session.init-conflict-retry.test.ts:94-98). Upstream retries it (up to 5 attempts with backoff); with zero content the bridge classifies it session_init_conflict so its own bounded auto-retry can key on it.

payload.errorMessage: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:atrium:chat:u-testuser01:own-chat; please retry your message.

init-conflict-zero-content-9.36.description: src/auto-reply/reply/session-init-conflict-retry.ts:12 (message verbatim; upstream test src/auto-reply/reply/session.init-conflict-retry.test.ts:110,122) — the pre-generation OCC init conflict as worded 7.1->9.36, with no trailing sentence. Same contract: session_init_conflict.
init-conflict-zero-content-9.36.only_at_why: v2026.10.33 appends `; please retry your message.` to the message (init-conflict-zero-content).

compaction-explicit-stream-signals.description: src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-compaction.test.ts:42 + src/plugins/wired-hooks-compaction.test.ts:126-134,208-217 — the EXPLICIT mid-turn compaction signal: {stream:'compaction', phase:'start'} then {phase:'end', outcome:'completed', willRetry:true, completed:true}. The overflow retry replays inside the SAME runId with no lifecycle end; accumulated text must survive. NOTE 2026.9.1: start/end also carry an optional itemId correlating one compaction operation (src/agents/sessions/agent-session-compaction.ts:182-183,214) — not read by the bridge.

chat-append-only-deltas.description: ui/src/api/gateway-chat-events.node.test.ts:29-87 — the WIRE of the append-only live text (2026.9.7 on, unchanged at v2026.10.33), verbatim from the Control UI's own test: one delta carrying the cumulative `message`, then deltas carrying `deltaText` only (`projectChatWireDelta`, src/gateway/server-chat-live-text.ts:17-21), a `replace` and a fresh append. The bridge restores `message` at the connection (live-text-baseline.ts, mirroring `mergeChatStreamMessage`, packages/gateway-client/src/chat-stream-message.ts:4-46). CONTRACT: projected, the live text grows to "Hello world" and ends on "New answer"; raw, it would freeze on "Hello".

chat-delta-after-terminal-no-baseline.description: ui/src/api/gateway-chat-events.node.test.ts:155-233 — a terminal retires the run's baseline, so a later append-only delta has nothing to append to; the Control UI closes the socket on it ("chat stream baseline missing"). At v2026.10.33 the test is a table over which boundary retires an OWNED baseline (final, aborted, error, unsubscribe); the `final` row is this scenario. CONTRACT: the bridge reports the gap and forwards the frame WITHOUT its fragment.

agent-assistant-append-only.description: src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts:2341,2378 — the agent stream's append-only wire, as the gateway's own test pins it: `{text:"one",delta:"one"}` then `{delta:" two"}` (`projectAssistantWireDelta`, server-chat-live-text.ts:23-28), then the final carrying "one two". The lifecycle end and the final's envelope are ours. CONTRACT: the second frame reaches the reader with `data.text` "one two"; the turn completes with "one two".

Its text names no storage fact a classifier could rely on, so only the structured kind can classify it. CONTRACT: finalize error, errorKind gateway_state_contention (never auto-retried).

status-waiting-for-state-then-resume.description: ui/src/pages/chat/chat-gateway.contention.test.ts:60-80 — the quiet wait as the Control UI's own test hands it to its chat handler (past the socket's baseline reconstruction, so the resuming delta shows `deltaText` only): a `status` frame with phase `waiting_for_state`, then that delta on the same run. chat-delta-replace-retracts-text.description: src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts:1053-1085 — NEW reading at v2026.10.33: text already shown is TAKEN BACK mid-run. The gateway's own test streams "Provisional answer", replaces the item, and pins three chat payloads: the delta, a delta `replace:true` with an empty `deltaText` and an EMPTY message text, then a `final` with NO `message`. The same frame shape is what a transcript commit sends when it retires recorded text from the live buffer (src/gateway/server-chat-transcript-publication.ts:222-230). The payloads are the test's matcher; `role`, the block `type` and the seq are ours. CONTRACT: after the replace the live text is empty, not the retired text; the turn ends final.

run-status-retrying-reason-retry-at.description: src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts:569-614 — NEW at v2026.10.33: a provider back-off says WHY and UNTIL WHEN. The gateway's test emits `run_status` {phase:'retrying', attempt, maxAttempts:10, reason, retryAt} for the reasons `rate_limit` and `timeout`, and pins the chat status it derives: state:'status', phase:'starting_model', retry {attempt, maxAttempts, reason, retryAt}. One attempt of that loop (attempt 2, reason `timeout` — refused as a retry reason through v2026.9.36, whose schema knows `rate_limit` only); the delta and the final after it are ours. CONTRACT: the turn enters a `retrying` phase carrying the reason and the retryAt, is not finalized by it, then completes.

chat-send-ack-accepted-queued.description: src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-queued-identity.test.ts:115-120 — NEW at v2026.10.33: a send put in the follow-up queue stores `{runId, status:"accepted"}` as its key's replayable answer, so a repeated key reads `accepted` where v2026.9.36 answered `in_flight`. This is an RPC answer, not an event: it sits in `ack`, and `frames` is empty. CONTRACT: `accepted` means the gateway HOLDS the input, like `started` and `in_flight`.
